key_catalysts.event: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook — the first edition to incorporate the 7-8 July ceasefire breach
key_catalysts.rationale: The July STEO was released on 7 July 2026, coincident with the breach and not reflecting it, and forecasts Brent averaging $74/bbl in Q3 2026 and $65/bbl in 2027 against a spot of $91.82. A material upward revision would validate the terms-of-trade channel that carries a 0.16 strategic weight and would confirm that the energy contribution to US headline inflation persists into Q4.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — the market is anchored on the stale $74 Q3 forecast
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/NOK and USD/CAD directly; EUR/USD, USD/JPY and USD/SGD through the importer-versus-exporter terms-of-trade channel

key_catalysts.event: US Consumer Price Index for July 2026
key_catalysts.rationale: The most important scheduled repricing event of the month. June's headline fell 0.4% month-on-month, the largest decline since April 2020, entirely because energy dropped 5.7% during the brief post-ceasefire oil collapse. Brent averaged $85 in June and traded between $86.99 and $105.32 through July, so the energy component mechanically reverses. We expect headline to re-accelerate toward 3.7-4.0% year-on-year with core near 2.6%.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — bank commentary describes Fed tightening expectations as having faded on the back of the June print, which we regard as a compositional error
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD above all, given EUR is 57.6% of the DXY and the asset-manager EUR long is +209,326 contracts

key_catalysts.rationale: Norges Bank held at 4.25% on 17 June but Governor Bache stated the rate "will be raised at one of the forthcoming monetary policy meetings" with a published forecast "just above 4.5 percent at the end of the year". A hike would take Norway 87.5bp above the Fed and, combined with Brent at $91.82 and a 15.59%-of-GDP surplus, would extend NOK's 4.37% July outperformance.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the guidance is explicit, but the timing between August, September and December is genuinely uncertain
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/NOK specifically; marginal for the DXY, since NOK carries no index weight

key_catalysts.event: Expiry of the 60-day no-charge Strait of Hormuz transit window under Article 5 of the 17 June US-Iran memorandum
key_catalysts.rationale: The memorandum granted safe passage "with no charge for 60 days only" from 17 June, so the window lapses around 16 August. Iran's lead negotiator has stated that "the administration of the strait will never return to the way that it was before the war" and has proposed transit fees. Because the United States is a net energy exporter, escalation delivers a haven bid and a terms-of-trade gain at the same time, while striking 71% of the DXY basket twice.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — there is no visible volatility kink at the mid-August tenor; the 1-week at 6.13 is a payroll premium, and 1-month is only 4.99
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: EUR/USD, USD/JPY and USD/SGD on the importer side; USD/NOK and USD/CAD on the exporter side

key_catalysts.event: Minutes of the 28-29 July FOMC meeting, and 50% Section 338 tariffs on approximately $20bn of Canadian goods take effect
key_catalysts.rationale: The minutes will reveal how close the Committee came to hiking, given three dissents in favour of a 25bp increase and a June record showing "many other participants" saw the appropriate end-2026 rate above the current range. The same date carries the Canadian Section 338 tariffs announced by USTR on 20 July with a thirty-day effective delay. Note the minutes date is derived from the Board's stated three-week rule rather than published.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the 9-3 vote is known but the internal distribution is not
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/CAD directly on the tariff leg; broad dollar on the minutes

key_catalysts.event: US Q2 GDP second estimate and July Personal Income and Outlays, including core PCE
key_catalysts.rationale: Core PCE is the Fed's target measure and stood at 3.3% year-on-year in June against a 2% goal, with the Dallas Fed trimmed mean at only 2.2%. A July core PCE at or above 3.3% alongside a Q2 GDP revision at or below 1.5% annualised is the stagflationary combination that most tests the Committee's stated intolerance of elevated inflation.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — the divergence between core PCE at 3.3% and trimmed mean at 2.2% is not a distinction the market currently trades
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: Broad dollar, with EUR/USD the primary conduit

key_catalysts.event: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, 27-29 August 2026, on "Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy"
key_catalysts.rationale: Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole. He has used every prior venue to reinforce the 2% commitment and has openly asked "how much accommodation are we getting from the balance sheet?", making balance-sheet policy a live topic in a year when reserves have fallen $355.2bn. Any signal that a September increase is on the table would validate the three dissenters and reprice the front end.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — the market has softened its Fed tightening expectations, so hawkish reinforcement is an upside surprise
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: Broad dollar; largest impact on USD/JPY and EUR/USD

key_catalysts.event: Bank of Canada and Reserve Bank of New Zealand policy decisions on the same day
key_catalysts.rationale: The BoC is expected to hold at 2.25% with CPI-trim at 1.8% and unemployment at 6.5%, preserving a 137.5bp dollar advantage. The RBNZ, having hiked 25bp to 2.50% on 8 July and stated that "further OCR increases appear likely at upcoming meetings", is more likely than not to hike again, narrowing the dollar's 112.5bp advantage.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — an RBNZ hike is well telegraphed; a BoC hold is fully priced
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: USD/CAD and NZD/USD; both outside or marginal to the DXY

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision and Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The pivotal event of the horizon. The June SEP median for end-2026 is 3.8%, implying one hike, and three members already voted for it on 29 July. September is the first meeting with an updated dot plot and is therefore the venue at which the Committee must either deliver or visibly abandon its own median. We also expect scrutiny of the 2027 median of 3.6%, which embeds a cut we regard as the least credible element of the projections.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — the 1-year bill at 4.08% against a 3.63% effective rate implies roughly 45bp of tightening over twelve months, so some hike probability is embedded, but not a September delivery specifically
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: All dollar pairs; EUR/USD carries the largest index weight and USD/JPY the largest rate beta

key_catalysts.rationale: Funding for the federal government lapses at the end of the fiscal year. 2026 has already produced a partial Department of Homeland Security shutdown running from 14 February to 30 April, so the base rate for disruption is empirically high rather than theoretical. The same date carries the expiry of surface transportation and Export-Import Bank authorisations.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — shutdown risk carries no visible premium in FX volatility at that tenor
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: Broad dollar; historically most visible in USD/CHF and USD/JPY through the haven channel

key_catalysts.rationale: All 435 House seats and one third of the Senate are contested, determining the fiscal and trade policy settings for the remainder of the presidential term. Given that judicial rulings have already voided the IEEPA tariff architecture and left roughly $166bn of refunds in dispute, congressional control has unusually direct implications for the revenue path that underpins the term premium currently sitting in the 30-year at 5.27%.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Not priced — the one-year EUR/USD implied volatility of 5.98 embeds no election premium
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: Broad dollar, with the transmission running through the long end rather than the front end

key_catalysts.event: Simultaneous expiry of three US-China suspensions: certain Section 301 tariff exclusions, the BIS Affiliates Rule and the Section 301 shipbuilding remedy
key_catalysts.rationale: All three were suspended to a common date under the trade arrangement. China's side of the arrangement included eliminating global export controls on rare earths, and Beijing added ten US firms to its own export-control list on 22 June after the Pentagon listed roughly 80 Chinese companies. A failure to extend would re-escalate the trade conflict at a moment when the tariff architecture is already under appeal.
key_catalysts.bilateral_relevance: Broad dollar and the Asian complex, most directly USD/SGD given Singapore's role as a regional trade hub

key_catalysts.event: FOMC decision and the year's final Summary of Economic Projections
key_catalysts.rationale: The last opportunity for the Committee to deliver the 3.8% end-2026 median from the June SEP. If no hike has been delivered by then, the December projections must either mark down the 2026 median or carry an unfulfilled commitment into 2027 — either outcome is a credibility event for a Chair who has staked his tenure on price stability.
key_catalysts.priced_in: Partially — embedded in the 45bp of tightening implied by the 1-year bill, but with no meeting-specific pricing observable from free sources

factors_changed.reason: The strategic stance turns Bullish because the DXY-weighted carry arithmetic — +147bp, falling only to +118bp under an aggressive peer-tightening stress test — proved more durable than the prior cycle's equally weighted read. Tactical confidence falls 10 points because the Fed has still not delivered the hike its own median implies while the RBA, RBNZ and Norges Bank have moved.

Both horizons deteriorate. Q2 GDP came in at 1.5% annualised against 2.1% in Q1, June payrolls were 57,000 with 74,000 of back revisions, and euro-area growth of 0.4% q/q has closed the exceptionalism gap. Meanwhile core CPI decelerated from 2.9% to 2.6% and the trimmed mean is only 2.2%, so the inflation overshoot is narrower than the prior cycle assumed.

Direction unchanged, confidence reduced on both horizons. The regime is still goldilocks with the S&P 500 at a record 7,489.72 and IG at 80bp, but the unresolved Hormuz situation makes the left tail materially fatter than it was in June, and a net-energy-exporter United States benefits doubly in that branch.

Both horizons take a stance where the prior cycle had none. Tactically, specs added 1,583 USD Index contracts into the 28 July high and the composite leveraged short in foreign currency reached -240,642 — a crowded long. Strategically, IMF COFER showed the dollar's reserve share rising to 57.13% and TIC recorded $262.8bn of monthly long-term inflows, both new information since the prior cycle.

The largest single stance reversal in the dossier, and the one that drives the strategic score inversion. Brent rose from roughly $70 on 26 June to $91.82 on 27 July with a $105.32 intramonth peak, and the Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack spread reached $63.61 — an unambiguous terms-of-trade transfer to a net energy exporter that was simply not present at the prior valuation date when oil was near $79 and falling.

The strategic stance turns Bullish on evidence unavailable in June: three dissents in favour of a hike on 29 July against a unanimous 12-0 hold on 17 June, the deliberate removal of the easing bias documented in the June minutes, five external task forces announced on 9 July, and the Chair's flat statement that "there is no soft inflation target".

The tactical stance flips from Bearish to Bullish because the escalation branch is now the dominant near-dated binary and it resolves dollar-positive: the ceasefire was breached on 7-8 July, Iran re-announced closure, and the Article 5 no-charge transit window expires around 16 August. In June the operative assumption was that the ceasefire framework would hold.

Fiscal risk has become tactically live for the first time in this series. The 30-year reached 5.27% and the 20-year 5.28% on 31 July with breakevens flat at 2.28%, the FY2026 year-to-date deficit reached $1.367tn, and the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling removed roughly $1.7tn of projected tariff revenue that the CBO baseline still assumes.

A full tactical reversal driven by price: the DXY made a 52-week high at 101.80, failed, and broke the 100 handle on 30 July with a -1.01% session. Confidence falls on both horizons because the moving averages and the implied-volatility percentile are estimates this cycle rather than measured values.

The tactical stance turns Bullish because reserve scarcity has become measurable: reserves at $2.945tn are down $355.2bn year-on-year, the ON RRP is drained to roughly $2bn, the TGA hit $998bn, and SOFR is printing exactly at IORB with a 3.70% 75th percentile. The strategic stance stays Neutral because the Fed's bill-purchase directive and TGA normalisation offset the drain over the horizon.

seasonality.pattern: Quarter-end and year-end US dollar funding pressure. Repo and cross-currency funding costs reliably firm into 30 September and 31 December as dealer balance sheets contract for regulatory reporting dates, and the effect is amplified when bank reserves are scarce. The mechanism is documented and observable: reserve balances stood at $2,944,541mn on 29 July, down $355,152mn year-on-year on a Wednesday-to-Wednesday basis, with the ON RRP buffer drained to roughly $2bn and SOFR already printing exactly at the 3.65% interest rate on reserve balances with a 75th percentile of 3.70%.
seasonality.relevance_window: Directly relevant within the strategic horizon: the 30 September quarter-end falls two months out and the 31 December year-end five months out, both inside the one-to-six-month window. Not relevant to the two-to-four-week tactical horizon.

The observable base for the current cycle is that SOFR is at IORB with a 3.70% 75th percentile before any quarter-end effect has been applied.
seasonality.current_alignment: Aligned with the tactical Bullish stance on Factor 10 and with the strategic Neutral stance, since the seasonal tightening lands at the same time as the Treasury General Account normalises from a $997.9bn late-July peak toward the guided $950bn end-September balance — the two forces partly offset. The 30 September appropriations expiry sits on the same date, so any funding-market stress that quarter would be compounded by a fiscal event.

The implied-volatility surface rests on a SINGLE dealer's mid — Saxo Bank OTC FX Options Analytics, snapped at 07:00 GMT on 31 July 2026 (a London-morning mark, not a New York close). CME CVOL was unobtainable across six endpoints, the CBOE EVZ index has been discontinued since 11 March 2025, and no second-dealer corroboration was available. All implied vols and risk reversals in this dossier carry that single-source caveat.

The 1-year implied-volatility percentile of approximately 20 is an ESTIMATE. No continuous one-year implied-vol history was retrievable, so the percentile is inferred from the absolute level of 4.99 against a year that contained a war, a Strait of Hormuz closure and a 40bp move in ten-year yields.

Three-month implied volatility was obtainable only for EUR/USD (5.25). The carry-to-volatility ratios for JPY, CHF, CAD and AUD use 1-month implied vols as a proxy (7.65, 6.52, 4.03 and 7.23 respectively) and the SEK ratio uses the cache's 20-day realised vol of 7.29% as a proxy. The ratios are therefore rank-ordering devices rather than precise measurements.

CROSS-CURRENCY BASIS IS A HARD GAP. The 3-month EUR/USD and USD/JPY cross-currency bases — the framework's designated benchmarks for global dollar funding — are dealer-quoted OTC instruments and were not obtainable from BIS, the ECB, the BoJ, the Federal Reserve, FRED or any free venue. Factor 10 substitutes the SOFR-IORB spread (0bp), central bank liquidity swaps outstanding ($132mn) and standing repo facility usage ($3mn), all of which indicate no offshore stress. Factor 10 strategic confidence is held to 50 on this basis.

OIS-implied policy probabilities are a HARD GAP. No CME FedWatch or OIS-derived meeting probability series was retrievable. Wherever the dossier refers to a market-implied path it uses the Treasury bill curve as an explicit proxy — the 1-year bill at 4.08% against a 3.63% effective funds rate implies roughly 45bp of tightening over twelve months — and says so. Bill yields embed a term premium, so this proxy overstates the pure policy expectation by an unknown amount.

Secondary aggregators show Moody's Aa1 stable and S&P AA+ stable and disagree with each other on Fitch, so no Fitch rating is asserted anywhere in this dossier. No sovereign CDS quote was obtainable. This is a real-effective-rate relative-valuation proxy for PPP and is labelled as such. The BIS REER historical percentile of 43 is likewise an estimate, since BIS publishes levels rather than percentiles.
